result.title: Automated Assembly Instruction Generation from CAD Models Using Grounded Large Language Models: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework
result.summary: Assembly documentation is a downstream manufacturing artifact that is still usually authored by interpreting CAD models by hand. Structured product data and large language models are both available, yet studies of CAD interpretation, assembly sequence planning, instruction writing, and human oversight have largely proceeded separately. This paper formulates CAD-grounded assembly instruction generation: the production of natural-language assembly procedures constrained by structured engineering information extracted from CAD models. The proposed framework maps a STEP assembly to a typed ProductGraph intermediate representation, derives a precedence order by deterministic topological sorting, realizes each step as language conditioned only on selected graph context, attaches per-step visual documentation, and applies rule-based and model-assisted checks. PDF export remains disabled until a human reviewer resolves every quality flag. The case study establishes endto-end feasibility on a built-in six-part reference assembly: the pipeline preserves a reported assembly order and carries quantity, material, and torque into an exported manual page. Generalization and geometric validation remain open empirical questions. The contribution is an architecture that separates engineering state, deterministic reasoning, grounded language realization, verification, and human release.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究从 CAD 模型（STEP 装配）自动生成装配说明书：将模型映射为类型化 ProductGraph 中间表示，用确定性拓扑排序导出工序顺序，每步仅基于选定的图上下文生成语言并附视觉文档，再经规则与模型校验，直到人工审阅清除全部质量标记后才导出 PDF，并在六零件参考装配上验证端到端可行性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「结构化状态—确定性推理—受限语言实现—校验—人工放行」的分层架构，可能为 LVR 中推理状态的显式表示、答案对证据的受限使用以及停止/放行决策提供可核查的方法线索，但领域相距较远，迁移性尚需判断。
